title: SR-1.10 A suite that is green on any machine
request: Closes G10: 12 tests need ssh-keygen, 8 need an authenticated gh and network, 3 fail when MEMEV_NO_SERVICE is set. Repository: memev. Depends on contracts: none.

tasks.title: Native OpenSSH keys and signatures
requirements: deploy keys are made with node:crypto in OpenSSH format
SSHSIG sign and verify are implemented in Node; ssh-keygen is not spawned

the native verify follows the allowed_signers rules of ssh-keygen -Y verify: one line whose principal pattern matches the principal and whose key is the signer's, '#' comments ignored, namespaces= and valid-before= honoured, and hash_alg limited to sha256 and sha512
agentid-bind.mjs signs, verifies and reads public keys in Node with no program on PATH, and no module under src/ runs ssh-keygen
a signature memev writes is byte-identical to what ssh-keygen -Y sign writes for the same key, namespace and message, so a third party's ssh-keygen -Y verify accepts it
the deploy key is written in openssh-key-v1 format, created at mode 0600 with no wider window, and never overwrites a key that exists

verify accepts the key types ssh-keygen accepts in bindings today (RSA with rsa-sha2-512, ECDSA P-256, Ed25519 and the security-key forms) and both hash algorithms; signing with a key the native signer cannot use fails with a named AgentBindError before anything is written
docs/MODULES.md is rewritten with node scripts/docs/module-graph.mjs, and docs/AGENT-IDENTITY.md and docs/THREAT-MODEL.md describe the native sign and verify

each red-green criterion of this task that runs test/sshsig.test.mjs has its own subtest whose name starts with <task>-cNN: (NN is the criterion's position in this task, so T1-c01: for the first), and the criterion runs only that subtest

criteria.statement: Signatures interoperate with ssh-keygen -Y verify fixtures

criteria.statement: test/sshsig.test.mjs holds ssh-keygen-made fixtures inline (ed25519 keys A and B, signatures in namespace memev over one binding message). Through both the sshsig.mjs verify and verifyAgentBinding, it asserts: with allowed_signers 'alice A' and 'bob B', a signature by B is rejected as -I alice and accepted as -I bob; principal 'ali' does not match a line for 'alice'; a line '# alice A' does not authorise A; 'alice namespaces="git" A' and 'alice valid-before="20200101" A' reject; 'bob,alice A' accepts -I alice; a blob whose hash_alg is not sha256 or sha512 rejects; a namespace 'other' signature rejects.

criteria.statement: The test is given, inline, an unencrypted ed25519 private key made by ssh-keygen and the armored output of `ssh-keygen -Y sign -n memev` with that key over a fixed binding message. The module's signer must produce exactly the same armored bytes (Ed25519 is deterministic, and ssh-keygen hashes with sha512 by default). The same message signed in namespace 'other' must give different bytes, equal to a second fixture.

criteria.statement: A test in test/agentid-bind.test.mjs sets process.env.PATH to an empty directory. With an inline ed25519 fixture key, bindAgentRole and setupAgentRole then succeed, verifyAgentBinding returns 'bound' for the binding and 'invalid' for principal 'bob', and setupAgentRole with a second fixture key throws code 'conflict'. It is red at base for the right reason: base throws code 'openssh' (src/engine/agentid-bind.mjs:93-96) and returns 'unavailable' (:181).

From an unencrypted ed25519 key made by ssh-keygen (inline fixture), take its seed, checkint and comment. Given those, the module's OpenSSH key writer must write the private key byte for byte equal to the fixture, and a .pub line equal to the fixture's .pub. A freshly made key must parse as openssh-key-v1 with cipher and kdf none, two equal checkints, a public blob equal to the .pub's, a 64-byte seed||pub private field whose seed reproduces the public key through node:crypto, padding 1,2,3..., and a .pub line of the form 'ssh-ed25519 <base64> <comment>'.

criteria.statement: With inline ssh-keygen fixtures: verify accepts signatures made with rsa-sha2-512 (RSA 3072), ecdsa-sha2-nistp256 and ed25519 security keys (the sk- key type), and one made with -O hashalg=sha256. Signing with the RSA fixture gives exactly ssh-keygen's bytes (PKCS#1 v1.5 is deterministic). Signing with a passphrase-protected ed25519 fixture either succeeds, with the passphrase supplied through the module's prompt hook, and matches ssh-keygen's bytes, or throws an AgentBindError with a named code before anything is written. It never stores a signature that fails verification.

tasks.title: No network or real gh in tests
requirements: tests that touch GitHub use the fake gh on PATH and a local bare remote
service tests set their own env
every test that runs git sets GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL to a file of its own and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, through one helper, so a person's url.insteadOf, signing or hook settings never reach a test
no test reaches a real gh, ssh, ssh-keygen or service manager, or the network: the suite passes with logging shims for them first on PATH and only loopback up
no test is deleted, renamed, skipped or marked todo to make the suite pass; the hermetic run reports fail 0, cancelled 0, todo 0 and only the skips that need MEMEV_CONTRACT_BASE
the one git helper also keeps system config away (GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1), so a person's hooks path, signing and URL rewrites never reach a test, and the two file:// tests keep file:// remotes

each service test sets MEMEV_NO_SERVICE itself, or clears it and injects both the platform and the runner, so the suite passes whether or not the caller exports it and no test reaches a real service manager

test/helpers/no-network.mjs, loaded with node --import, makes every net, tls, dgram and dns connection attempt to anything but loopback throw, and sandbox() in test/helpers/cli.mjs passes the caller's NODE_OPTIONS through to the processes it starts

criteria.statement: The suite passes with no network, no ssh-keygen and a bare environment

verifier.cmd: H=$(mktemp -d) && env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:$(dirname $(command -v node)) HOME=$H MEMEV_NO_SERVICE=1 npm test

criteria.statement: Shims for gh, ssh, ssh-keygen, launchctl, systemctl, loginctl and schtasks come first on PATH. Each appends its argv to a log and exits 127. The suite runs with a fresh HOME and NODE_OPTIONS loading test/helpers/no-network.mjs, which makes every net, tls, dgram and dns connection attempt to anything but loopback throw (a fixture test that opens a socket fails under it and passes without it); it passes, and the log stays empty.

A hostile global and system config is planted: a file:// rewrite, commit and tag signing with gpg.program=false, and a core.hooksPath whose hooks log and fail. A pre-check first proves git can see the planted config. The suite passes with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, XDG_CONFIG_HOME and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM unset in the caller and GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM pointing at the hostile file; no planted hook ran; and both file:// tests still use file://.

verifier.cmd:
H=$(mktemp -d) && mkdir $H/hooks && printf '#!/bin/sh
echo "$0" >> %s/hooklog
exit 1
' "$H" > $H/hooks/pre-commit && cp $H/hooks/pre-commit $H/hooks/pre-push && chmod +x $H/hooks/* && printf '[url "ssh://example.invalid/"]
	insteadOf = file://
[commit]
	gpgsign = true
[tag]
	gpgsign = true
[gpg]
	program = false
[core]
	hooksPath = %s/hooks
' "$H" > $H/.gitconfig && cp $H/.gitconfig $H/system && test "$(env -u GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL HOME=$H git config --global --get gpg.program)" = false && env -u GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL -u XDG_CONFIG_HOME -u GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=$H/system MEMEV_NO_SERVICE=1 HOME=$H npm test && test ! -e $H/hooklog && grep -q 'file://' test/backup-remote.test.mjs && grep -q 'file://' test/relay-fallback.test.mjs

criteria.statement: With MEMEV_NO_SERVICE unset in the caller and logging shims for launchctl, systemctl, loginctl and schtasks first on PATH, the suite passes and no shim was reached. This proves each service test sets its own env, in both directions. Tests that bring their own fake service manager (test/service-sandbox.test.mjs:43) put it ahead of the shims.

verifier.cmd:
S=$(mktemp -d) && for b in launchctl systemctl loginctl schtasks; do printf '#!/bin/sh
echo "$0 $*" >> %s/log
exit 127
' "$S" > "$S/$b" && chmod +x "$S/$b"; done && env -u MEMEV_NO_SERVICE PATH="$S:$PATH" HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm test && test ! -s "$S/log"

criteria.statement: The suite passes with a git URL rewrite and commit signing set in the user's global git config

verifier.cmd:
H=$(mktemp -d) && printf "[url "ssh://example.invalid/"]
	insteadOf = file://
[commit]
	gpgsign = true
" > $H/.gitconfig && MEMEV_NO_SERVICE=1 HOME=$H npm test

criteria.statement: Every test( title in the test files at the contract's base (test/*.test.mjs, and test/docs/*.test.mjs once SR-1.33 has moved document checks there) is still present at head; this contract allows no title to be replaced. In the hermetic environment the TAP summary shows fail 0, cancelled 0, todo 0 and at most 2 skipped (the two MEMEV_CONTRACT_BASE skips at test/hooks-startup.test.mjs:100 and :114; counted statically).

verifier.cmd: B="$MEMEV_CONTRACT_BASE"; [ -n "$B" ] || { echo 'MEMEV_CONTRACT_BASE is not set'; exit 2; }; R='^test\([^,]*'; t0=$(mktemp); t1=$(mktemp); tap=$(mktemp); for f in $(git ls-tree -r --name-only "$B" test/ | grep -E '^test/(docs/)?[^/]+[.]test[.]mjs$'); do git show "$B:$f" | grep -oE "$R"; done | sort -u > "$t0" && cat $(ls test/*.test.mjs test/docs/*.test.mjs 2>/dev/null) | grep -oE "$R" | sort -u > "$t1" && test -z "$(comm -23 "$t0" "$t1")" && env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:$(dirname $(command -v node)) HOME=$(mktemp -d) MEMEV_NO_SERVICE=1 node --test --test-concurrency=4 --test-reporter=tap $(ls test/*.test.mjs test/docs/*.test.mjs 2>/dev/null) > "$tap"; grep -qx '# fail 0' "$tap" && grep -qx '# cancelled 0' "$tap" && grep -qx '# todo 0' "$tap" && grep -qE '^# skipped [0-2]$' "$tap"
